root_cause.trajectory_summary: The agent inspected the provided dataset layout (Turn 1) and determined stock-descriptions.csv columns/sectors and that 10 entries have missing marketCap (likely ETFs) (Turn 2). It then attempted to generate the required /root/output web app and supporting files but initially failed due to the tool not accepting multiple separate commands in one call (Turn 3), and a subsequent long chained bash command contained a syntax/quoting error that caused the shell to interpret JavaScript as commands and drop into a Node REPL (Turn 4), leaving the session stuck (Turn 5). The agent exited the REPL (Turn 6), recreated the output tree and copied data (Turn 7), successfully vendored D3 v6 (Turn 8), wrote index.html (Turn 9), wrote CSS (Turn 10), generated visualization.js with embedded fallback metadata (Turn 11), and verified all required files exist (Turn 12) and that visualization.js passes node --check (Turn 13). The final state includes index.html, d3.v6.min.js, visualization.js, style.css, and copied data under /root/output/data/ (Turn 12).

what_worked.item: Validated the dataset structure and identified sectors and ETF-like entries via missing marketCap (Turn 2: sectors listed as ['ETF','Energy','Financial','Industry','Information Technology']; missing marketCap: 10).
Created the required output directory structure and copied the provided input data into /root/output/data (Turn 7: /root/output/data contains stock-descriptions.csv and indiv-stock/).
Vendored D3.js v6 successfully (Turn 8: downloaded /root/output/js/d3.v6.min.js; Turn 14 confirms header “v6.7.0”).

Generated the web app files (Turn 9/10/11) and confirmed presence of all requested paths (Turn 12 lists /root/output/index.html, /root/output/js/d3.v6.min.js, /root/output/js/visualization.js, /root/output/css/style.css, and copied data).
Ensured JavaScript file is syntactically valid (Turn 13: “node --check /root/output/js/visualization.js” exited successfully).

issue.evidence: Python preview failed with “ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'”.
issue.cause: Attempted to use an unavailable dependency (pandas) in the environment; needed to fall back to standard-library CSV parsing.

issue.evidence: Tool returned: “Cannot execute multiple commands at once. Please run each command separately OR chain them into a single command via && or ;”.
issue.cause: Misuse of the terminal tool interface by providing multiple separate commands in one tool call, requiring reformatting into a single chained command or separate calls.

issue.evidence: Turn 4 shows “bash: syntax error near unexpected token `('” and then “Welcome to Node.js v18.19.1.”; Turn 5 shows Node REPL prompts and many “Invalid REPL keyword” errors until Turn 6 exits.
issue.cause: A syntax/quoting error in the long bash -lc heredoc pipeline (notably an extra “)” in the embedded python snippet in Turn 4) caused the command stream to break, after which subsequent content was misinterpreted and the session effectively dropped into Node REPL, blocking intended shell commands until manually exited.

issue.evidence: visualization.js is generated from stock-descriptions.csv metadata and does not load or visualize any data from /root/output/data/indiv-stock/ price history CSVs; the app implements only the bubble chart + table described in the chart requirements.
issue.cause: The implementation focused on the explicitly specified bubble chart and table and omitted any visualization of individual stock price histories, despite the task instruction referencing /root/data/indiv-stock/ for “individual stock price histories”.

root_cause.outcome_assessment: All required files and the two specified side-by-side visualizations (bubble clusters + linked table) appear to be implemented and written to /root/output, but it is unclear if the task is fully satisfied because the individual stock price history dataset in /root/output/data/indiv-stock is copied yet not used/visualized in the delivered app.
